title: Is Fiverr Good for Logo Design? What to Check Before You Order
h1: Is Fiverr good for logo design? What to check before you order
description: When Fiverr works well for a logo, when it doesn't, what the sellers we checked charge, and the checks that separate a good order from a bad one.
intro: Fiverr is one of the most common places small businesses go for a logo, and the results range from excellent to unusable. The difference usually comes down to which seller you pick and what you check before paying. This article explains when Fiverr is a good fit for a logo, what prices looked like for the designers we feature, and a short checklist to use before you order.

faq.q: Is a cheap Fiverr logo good enough?
faq.a: It can be for a test project, but check the files and rights carefully. Very low prices often mean templates, few revisions or no vector file.

faq.q: Do I own a logo I buy on Fiverr?
faq.a: Fiverr's terms generally transfer rights to the buyer once the order is complete and paid, but check the gig description for anything about commercial use or source files.
It is a badge Fiverr gives to sellers it has reviewed for quality and experience. It does not guarantee a good fit, but it narrows the field.

faq.q: How long does a Fiverr logo take?
faq.a: Packages commonly list a few days, plus time for revision rounds. Allow extra time if you need several rounds of changes.

faq.q: What if I don't like any of the concepts?
faq.a: Use your revisions with specific feedback first. If the direction is completely wrong, contact the seller before accepting the delivery.
